PullRequest.Title: voice: remove the unused Voice Mode floating window
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Removes the Voice Mode floating (auxiliary) window. It has been unreachable since #322608 removed the command and setting that opened it. #320785 added the window, and #321957 removed the in-chat voice bar that set its focus context key, but neither of the later PRs removed the implementation.

### Removed

- From `contrib/agentsVoice/browser/`: the window service, the widget and its binding, the sessions picker, the whole `components/` folder, and the voice event stream view, whose contribution was never imported.
- `contrib/agentsVoice/electron-browser/agentsVoiceNativeCommands.ts` and its import in `workbench.desktop.main.ts`.
- Code that only the window used:
  - `IAgentsVoiceWindowService`, the window size constants, and the `WindowOpen`, `WindowBounds` and `OnboardingCompleted` storage keys.
  - `submitFeedback` on `IVoiceSessionController` and `IVoiceClientService`, plus the feedback payload types. The window's feedback dialog was the only caller.
  - `IVoiceSessionController.markUserCancelled` and the state-change suppression it fed.
  - The session controller's call to `_agentsVoice.openWindow`, a command that no longer exists.
  - `computeVoiceMicGlowBoxShadow`.
- `getSessionDescription` in `agentSessionsPicker.ts` is no longer exported, since it only has an internal use now.

### Hold to Talk hint

The idle "Hold {0} to talk" hints in the chat view and the Agents window chat inputs looked up the shortcut for `agentsVoice.pushToTalk`. That keybinding only matched while the removed window had focus, so it can never fire. The hints now look up `workbench.action.chat.voiceInputMode.holdToTalk`, the shortcut that works in the chat input and that the preview hint and Start Listening labels already use.

Both commands default to Ctrl+Shift+Space, so the hint text doesn't change by default. If someone rebinds Hold to Talk, the hint now shows the new shortcut. The unreachable `agentsVoice.pushToTalk` keybinding and the `agentsVoiceWidgetFocused` context key are removed. The Voice Mode: Push to Talk command stays in the Command Palette.

### Tests

- Removed the test that request cancellation preempts checkpoint playback; it only covered `markUserCancelled`.
- Cut 'request cancellation and disconnect cancel pending voice progress' down to its disconnect half.
- Removed the mic shadow assertion from `voiceGlow.test.ts`.

Scenarios.Scenario: Desktop startup and retirement of the legacy floating voice window, feedback dialog, and debug event-stream view
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Desktop module loading no longer imports the two native command registrations. The deleted window service was delayed and had no remaining registration consumer/open command; the event-stream contribution had no import. Their constructors, polling, rendering, feedback reads, and HTTP submission were not on a reachable startup path before this PR.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One desktop workbench startup per window. Deleted session-list, transcript-history, auxiliary-window, and polling work has zero effective runtime cardinality on the supported pre-diff paths.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Startup loses a module import and command registrations; no new parallel creation, polling, IPC, or cleanup is scheduled.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Removal does not add cache lookups or invalidations. The deleted service only cleared its obsolete persisted window-open flag; the remaining voice storage and transcript index are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: complete changed-file inventory and diff pages inspected, including all deleted implementations and the desktop import removal.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Any reduction in module-loading cost is unmeasured; unreachable deleted work is not counted as a demonstrated runtime performance improvement.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. Entire implementations and their callers are removed together; searches found no remaining references to the deleted window/widget/native-command/event-stream implementations. There is also insufficient evidence of an existing reachable performance regression being fixed to justify a regression-fix provenance report.

Scenarios.Scenario: Rendering the idle Hold to Talk hint in the chat view and Agents chat inputs
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing transcript autorun checks connection, input ownership, idle state, and transcript visibility, then performs one keybinding lookup and updates the hint before the existing scrollbar scan. Only the command ID passed to the lookup changes.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One lookup per eligible autorun execution on an owning empty idle input, not per transcript turn or animation frame. Existing transcript filtering, DOM replacement, and geometry scanning retain their previous frequency.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous local UI work on the existing autorun path. No new asynchronous operation, subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network call.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: AbstractKeybindingService.lookupKeybinding uses the shared keybinding resolver. WorkbenchKeybindingService caches that resolver until keybindings change; changing the queried command does not invalidate it or create a new cache. Cold resolver construction was possible for either command; warm lookup stays local.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both changed render branches and the lookup implementation/shared resolver cache were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of autorun executions depends on input activity, but that frequency and all layout work are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The diff changes the displayed shortcut source without adding work, listeners, render passes, or expensive boundaries.

Scenarios.Scenario: Voice-session state changes, request cancellation, narration, and disconnect across multiple chat sessions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing autoruns and session events inspect nonarchived agent sessions and resident chat models, deduplicate resources, and detect genuine transitions. Autorun transitions settle through one per-session pending map and a timer before context flush/narration. The removed cancellation-suppression map could only be populated by markUserCancelled, whose production callers were exclusively in the deleted window service. Live workflows therefore do not newly cross the previously guarded paths. Disconnect still stops capture/playback, disconnects the client, clears timers/maps, and disposes response watchers/model references.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize and send session-context updates over the existing voice connection; GPT Live uses its existing context comparison and append path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Standard context updates share a 500 ms debounce and a single aggregate delta for changed sessions, with zero WebSocket sends for an unchanged snapshot. Explicit flushes remain unchanged. GPT Live retains its existing comparisons before sending context appends.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical batching, snapshot comparison, serialization, and network calls on supported live workflows; the removed suppression map was never populated outside the removed window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Settled context is flushed before the existing narration request so the backend has authoritative state; ordinary context updates are deferred.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve cold remote chat-session content through its provider, including extension-host $provideChatSessionContent for extension-backed sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one in-flight eager load per distinct missing session key in the controller, further coalesced by ChatService and ChatSessionsService. Resident models and held eager references avoid another load. Distinct cold session keys can load concurrently; unsuccessful loads can be retried by later existing events.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same eager-load sites, per-key guards, shared in-flight resolution, and cross-key concurrency existed before the diff; suppression removal does not move or multiply them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold content can delay that session's detailed confirmation/completion narration, not all session processing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize a settled coding event, ensure the transcript directory exists, and append its JSONL record; update the existing storage index.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One append per accepted net state-change event with a user login. Autorun bursts collapse by session and net-zero changes are filtered before persistence. Each append performs the existing directory operation and append write.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same event cardinality and persistence calls on live workflows. Removing an unpopulated cancellation-suppression guard does not add writes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Persistence is issued without awaiting it on the narration path; the existing transcript-store shutdown join waits for pending writes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct tracked nonarchived agent-session resources plus resident non-agent chat models with requests, deduplicated by resource; settled transitions rather than every intermediate state drive persisted autorun events.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Local state scanning is synchronous. Autorun transitions coalesce per session using one settle timer; standard network context shares one debounce. Eager model work is coalesced per resource, not globally serialized. Transcript writes use one store-wide Sequencer. None of these concurrency controls changes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Previous session state, cached response summaries, pending narration, and last-sent context retain their existing deduplication and pruning. Eager loads reuse resident/held models and join in-flight requests. Removing cancellation-map cleanup matches removal of the map and all producers; other teardown remains intact.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: deleted producers/callers, every changed suppression branch, surviving coalescing, remote-load ownership, transcript persistence, and disconnect cleanup were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Session counts, provider latency, transcript-write duration, and event frequency vary; no measurements were taken. These uncertainties do not obscure a changed mechanism: the inspected boundary cardinality and placement are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The apparent broadening of stateChanges.push/cache invalidation is not an increase on reachable surviving paths because its suppression state could only be produced by deleted UI callers. No new retained resource, fan-out, or missing cleanup was established.

Scenarios.Scenario: Submitting voice transcription to a nonvisible target chat session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The controller checks the current target, awaits acquisition/loading if needed, and submits one chat request. The only removed operation on this path is the unawaited _agentsVoice.openWindow command after an accepted request. Response watching and reference ownership remain as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read a cold local target session from the existing chat-session store.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One acquisition attempt for the selected target per submission; a resident model returns an existing reference without a store read. No iteration over all sessions is added.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same acquisition and cold-store read occurred before submitting the same voice request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A cold local target must be restored before submitting the request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: For extension-backed remote targets, request session content across the extension-host boundary; existing request dispatch also reaches the selected chat provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selected target, with same-resource cold loads coalesced and resident content reused. One logical chat submission per utterance; existing steering/queued handling is retained.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical loading, in-flight joining, request dispatch, and request queue semantics. The additional legacy window command was invoked afterward and did not own the model reference.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold provider content must load before direct submission; the provider request starts the response. The deleted window command was unawaited and occurred only after acceptance.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One explicit or pinned target per submitted utterance; history length affects only the existing cold restoration. No new per-history-item or per-session boundary fan-out.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Acquisition precedes request dispatch within a submission; concurrent acquisitions of the same remote resource join. Existing per-session steering/queue behavior is unchanged. The removed fire-and-forget command does not add a wait or parallel burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing model references bypass cold loads. ChatService and ChatSessionsService join in-flight remote resolution by resource. Response references are still released on response stop, failure, stale generation, or disconnect. Existing response preview watchers still dispose on completion/cancellation or timeout.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed command removal, target routing, acquisition implementation, request submission, response watcher, and disconnect disposal were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual cold history sizes and remote provider latency are unknown, but both costs and their critical-path placement are unchanged by this PR.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The change removes an obsolete command invocation without changing expensive request/load scheduling or cleanup. Remaining response-preview work is pre-existing, not a diff-introduced performance issue.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass against base d208d7d2a09da7f1524b99c73fcb8adcfc2ec0d7. Inspected the complete 28-file inventory and all diff pages, then traced surviving UI, state-change, submission, cache/coalescing, expensive-boundary, and cleanup paths. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regressions found. No concrete reachable performance-regression fix met the provenance-reporting threshold. Static read-only review; runtime magnitudes were not measured.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
